**Yes, the cable can limit charging speed.** The charger and device negotiate power, but the cable's e-marker chip tells them how much current it can safely carry. Charging runs at the lowest of what the charger, the device, and the cable support.

**What the ratings mean**
- **60W (3A, 20V):** The basic rating. Most cables without an e-marker top out here.
- **100W (5A, 20V):** This needs an e-marked cable. USB-IF stopped certifying new 100W cables on December 22, 2021, and replaced the category with 240W. Many 100W cables are still sold, and they work fine for laptops up to 100W. [UL Solutions](https://www.ul.com/insights/240w-usb-c-cable-performance-testing-and-safety-considerations)
- **240W (5A, up to 48V, EPR):** This needs an e-marked cable. It covers 140W (28V), 180W (36V), and 240W (48V) power levels. [USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/usb-charger-pd)

USB-IF now says certified USB-C to USB-C cables must be labeled either 60W or 240W. [USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)

**How to check yours**
1. Look for a 60W or 240W logo on the cable or packaging.
2. Check the listed wattage and amps. 5A means e-marked.
3. If it has no markings, assume 60W.

**Things to keep in mind**
- A higher-rated cable won't make a slower charger or device charge faster. USB-IF notes a certified cable doesn't add to the capabilities of the products it connects. [USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)
- Charging speed and data speed are separate. A 240W cable can still be limited to USB 2.0 data (480 Mbps).

**Cable options**
- **Baseus USB-C to USB-C Cable, 100W (5A, e-marked):** from $9.99 for 1 m. It suits laptops up to 100W. It is charging-only (USB 2.0 data, no video), isn't rated for 140W or 240W, and Baseus says it doesn't support iPad Pro charging. The source didn't say whether it is USB-IF certified. [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-usb-c-cable-100w) (affiliate link, per the retailer's note). Details: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/usb-c-cable-60w-100w-240w-charging-speed-e-marker-usb-if-official)
- **For 240W:** USB-IF's certified list included 240W cables, such as the Bonelk 240W braided cable (480 Mbps data), but I don't have a purchase link or price for it. [USB-IF product list](https://www.usb.org/products)

**Bottom line:** Phones and tablets are fine on a 60W cable. For a laptop drawing 65-100W, use a 100W/5A e-marked cable. Only buy 240W if your charger and device both support above 100W.
